strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#24019 in pandas: rolling(5).corr/cov on a=[1e5,0,0,0,0] vs constant b=[9.45]*5 should give all-NaN corr and [nan,nan,nan,nan,0.0] cov, matching the developer's test_rolling_cov_corr_degenerate in pandas/tests/window/test_pairwise.py. Build pandas from the buggy commit 1d419237db25 with Cython extensions (aggregations.pyx), run the single parametrized test, expect failure on buggy and pass on fixed.

pinned_because: NumPy has no documented constraint and no era ceiling in the evidence; the strategy chooses a current NumPy compatible with the buggy commit's Cython build and states this as a choice, not a documented requirement

Cython is unpinned in the evidence (documented but no constraint); use the version the repo's build requirements at the commit specify, since the .pyx must be recompiled from the buggy and fixed revisions

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 1d419237db25, the parametrized test_rolling_cov_corr_degenerate fails: the corr case returns inf at the last position instead of nan, so tm.assert_series_equal against [nan]*5 fails, and the cov case may differ from [nan,nan,nan,nan,0.0]. On the fixed revision (the PR applying the incremental add_cov/remove_cov algorithm with numerically_unstable recompute and calc_corr returning NaN when ssqdm is 0.0), both parametrized cases pass.
strategy.numerical_probe: a = pd.Series([1e5,0,0,0,0]); b = pd.Series([9.45]*5); print(a.rolling(5).corr(b).tolist(), a.rolling(5).cov(b).tolist())

input_output_examples.input: a = pd.Series([1e5, 0, 0, 0, 0]); b = pd.Series([9.45] * 5); a.rolling(5).corr(b).iloc[4] vs a.corr(b)
a = pd.Series([1e5, 0, 0, 0, 0]); b = pd.Series([9.45] * 5); a.rolling(5).cov(b).iloc[4] vs a.cov(b)

risks: The buggy-vs-fixed transition depends on compiling aggregations.pyx at each revision; a stale build cache or an editable install not rebuilt after checkout will silently run the old extension, so rebuild after switching commits.

The defect is described as numerical instability tied to floating-point cancellation in the online co-moment update; it may only manifest on platforms where the arithmetic order or FMA contraction differs (e.g. some ARM or x86 builds with different compiler flags). The evidence does not state the platform, so the transition may not reproduce on every architecture; if it does not reproduce, check the compiler and -O flags first.
The evidence does not give a tolerance; the test uses exact tm.assert_series_equal, so the transition is decided by exact NaN vs inf and exact 0.0 equality, not by a tolerance.

The PR date and pandas version at the buggy commit are not given, so the exact NumPy/Cython versions that were in use cannot be recovered from the evidence; the chosen versions are a current-toolchain assumption.
Sanitisers or debug builds were not indicated; do not assume a sanitiser is needed for this transition.
Issue 24019 referenced in the test is an older issue number than the PR; the test file and the aggregations diff are the authoritative sources for the reproduction.

oracle.reference_source: pandas/tests/window/test_pairwise.py test_rolling_cov_corr_degenerate using tm.assert_series_equal against Series([nan]*5) and Series([nan,nan,nan,nan,0.0])
oracle.why: The developer test asserts exact series equality; no tolerance is stated in the evidence, so the transition is decided by exact NaN and exact 0.0 comparisons.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On buggy 1d419237db25 the corr case yields inf at index 4 where NaN is expected, so assert_series_equal against [nan]*5 raises an AssertionError; this is the failure the test is designed to catch.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the calc_corr path returns NaN when ssqdm_x or ssqdm_y is 0.0 and the cov path uses the incremental algorithm with numerically_unstable recompute, so both parametrized cases match their expected series exactly and the test passes.
